concept.title: Interval Property for Connected Slice-Projections of Polymatroids
concept.concept_description: For any connected polymatroid $P$ and any element $e$, the set of indices $j \in \{0, \dots, f(e)\}$ for which the $j$-th slice-projection of $e$ is connected forms a contiguous interval of integers. This conjecture strengthens the paper's theorem that no two consecutive slice-projections can both be disconnected, and naturally generalizes the interval property trivially satisfied by matroids (where the rank $f(e) \le 1$).
concept.mathematical_framing: For any connected polymatroid $P$ and any element $e$, the set of indices $j \in \{0, \dots, f(e)\}$ for which the $j$-th slice-projection of $e$ is connected forms a contiguous interval of integers. This conjecture strengthens the paper's theorem that no two consecutive slice-projections can both be disconnected, and naturally generalizes the interval property trivially satisfied by matroids (where the rank $f(e) \le 1$).
concept.lean_guess: Assume for contradiction that there exist indices $j < k < l$ such that the $j$-th and $l$-th slice-projections are connected, but the $k$-th is disconnected. Use the submodularity of the polymatroid rank function and the lattice of flats to demonstrate that if $P^{(k)}$ is disconnected by a partition $(A, B)$, then either $P^{(j)}$ or $P^{(l)}$ must also be disconnected by a related partition, contradicting the initial assumption.

concept.title: EML Fixed-Point Theorem: exp-log Iteration Convergence
concept.concept_description: The EML single operator f(x) = e^a * log(b*x + c) is a contraction mapping for suitable parameter ranges. Conjecture: For all a, b, c in R with a > 0 and b, c chosen so that the function maps a closed interval to itself, the iteration x_{n+1} = e^a * log(b*x_n + c) converges to a unique fixed point x* at a rate O(rho^n) where rho = |f'(x*)|. Moreover, the fixed point x* satisfies x* = e^a * log(b*x* + c) and can be expressed as a power series in a. The fixed point is unique because f is a contraction on the invariant interval: the derivative f'(x) = e^a * b / (b*x + c) is bounded by |f'| < 1 when the parameters are in the right range. This makes EML functions well-behaved iterative schemes, unlike arbitrary neural network activations. Test: prove convergence for the specific case a in (0,1), b=1, c in (0,1) and compute the fixed point explicitly as a series. Impact: establishes EML as having well-defined dynamical behavior, enabling EML-based iterative algorithms with certified convergence.

concept.title: Join-saturation equality for matchings with isolated vertices
concept.concept_description: For every integer t ≥ 1 and q ≥ 1, let F = tK₂ ∪ qK₁ be the disjoint union of a matching of size t and q isolated vertices. Then for every n > 2t + q, the Cameron--Puleo upper bound is tight: sat(n, K₁ ∨ F) = n - 1 + sat(n - 1, F). This extends the paper's proved cases t = 1 and t = 2 to all matchings with isolated vertices.
concept.mathematical_framing: For every integer t ≥ 1 and q ≥ 1, let F = tK₂ ∪ qK₁ be the disjoint union of a matching of size t and q isolated vertices. Then for every n > 2t + q, the Cameron--Puleo upper bound is tight: sat(n, K₁ ∨ F) = n - 1 + sat(n - 1, F). This extends the paper's proved cases t = 1 and t = 2 to all matchings with isolated vertices.
concept.lean_guess: The upper bound is exactly the Cameron--Puleo construction: take an extremal F-saturated graph on n-1 vertices and join one new universal vertex to it. For the lower bound, let G be any (K1∨F)-saturated graph on n vertices. Analyze a nonedge xy and the forced copy of K1∨F in G+xy. Because F is a matching plus isolated vertices, any forced copy can be decomposed into one apex vertex, t independent edges, and q remaining vertices avoiding the apex constraints. Show that the saturation condition forces either a universal vertex whose deletion is F-saturated, giving |E(G)| ≥ n-1+sat(n-1,F), or else enough local edge-disjoint matching witnesses around nonedges to yield the same global edge lower bound by degree counting. The base cases t=1,2 are supplied by the paper; the induction step increases t by removing one forced matching edge from each witness copy and applying the lower bound to the residual (t-1)K2∪qK1 configuration.
catalog_references: This paper: equality for F=K2∪qK1 and F=2K2∪qK1
